article:
By Alec McDonnell
BlackBerry CEO: Robotics is Tech’s Fastest-Growing Business
According to BlackBerry CEO John Giamatteo, robotics is one of the fastest-growing businesses within the tech industry, as the company begins to look toward AI as something to integrate within its own systems.
BlackBerry, once a major contender in the mobile and telecommunications market , has shifted from mobiles toward other software solutions over the years. One of the firm’s largest businesses is QNX, a safety-critical software platform used by vehicles.
The QNX platform provides operating systems and other embedded software to enhance vehicle features, such as braking systems and semi-autonomous driving functions.
The software has become a key player in safety-critical automotive software applications and is currently embedded in 275 million vehicles, according to BlackBerry.
BlackBerry's QNX safety-critical software is currently embedded in 275 million vehicles
The company is experiencing a backlog of QNX orders worth US$950m, with a significant portion attributed to robotics
In its first quarter, BlackBerry reported QNX revenue of US$72.3m, representing a 26% increase year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA for the QNX segment climbed 52% to US$19.3m
BlackBerry raised its full-year revenue outlook to a range of US$594m to US$621m
Robotics is going to shift in a hardcore way... and we couldn’t be more excited about the opportunity in front of us.
Amazon Web Services : BlackBerry co-developed BlackBerry IVY with AWS, leveraging cloud capabilities to process and analyse real-time connected vehicle data at scale.
Microsoft : BlackBerry integrates its Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) with Microsoft 365, enabling secure, managed access to productivity apps on enterprise mobile devices.
Google : BlackBerry collaborates with Google to enforce advanced security standards and zero-touch deployment for corporate Android Enterprise devices across organizations.
IBM : BlackBerry integrates with IBM's enterprise platforms to share threat intelligence, helping automate security workflows and accelerate Incident Response against cyber threats.
Meta Agrees to Platform Changes, Settling for US$17bn
Meta has agreed to implement major platform changes across Instagram and Facebook following its landmark child safety lawsuit .
Dozens of US states have previously accused the tech giant of creating addictive social media tools and subsequently harming child users.
The agreement will require Meta to pay up to US$17bn and the firm has also agreed to establish safeguards for younger users, including daily usage limits and blocks on nighttime use nationwide across the US.
This marks the first time ever that Meta has been required to change key features of the everyday user experience.
The jury trial, which took place in California, saw almost 30 states sue the US$1.36tn company over allegations that Meta deliberately designed addictive tools that hooked young people and caused them subsequent mental health-related issues.
NVIDIA Declares ‘Golden Age’ Amid 106% Revenue Growth
NVIDIA says quarterly revenue for the firm has more than doubled this year to nearly US$100bn.
Amid this news, Jensen Huang, NVIDIA’s CEO , says demand for the company’s services is accelerating as the AI industry reaches a new “golden age”.
NVIDIA – currently the most valuable firm in the world – brought in US$96.2bn in revenue, beating Wall Street expectations of US$92bn in the second quarter. In comparison, this quarter’s revenue was 106% higher than it was the same time last year.
“AI has reached its inflection point. It’s doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue,” Jensen says.
NVIDIA’s stock rose nearly 4% following the announcement and many investors consider the firm to be the predominant driving force for the entire AI industry.
Paramount Could Receive US$8bn for Sale of Turner Networks
Paramount Skydance could receive up to US$8bn and additional legal relief if it agrees to sell Warner Bros. Discovery’s Turner networks as it looks to settle two lawsuits challenging its acquisition of Warner Bros.
The US media giant, headed by David Ellison, has been trying to acquire Warner Bros. in a US$110bn deal since the beginning of this year.
While the deal has gained approval from jurisdictions around the world, many government officials and critics have cited concerns over the deal’s impact and potential harm on movie theatres, cable distributors and audiences.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who has taken the state’s case, says he wants considerable changes enacted with the deal before he agrees to settle the suit. Paramount says the firm is open to some form of structural agreement.
The Turner network owns TBS, TNT and CNN, which stand as some of the most valuable properties in the Warner Bros. portfolio. In total, they generate around US$2bn a year in earnings and analysts predict the business could sell for around four times those earnings.
Lego Explores New Product Areas Amid Record Profit Growth
Lego has announced plans to increase investment into new products such as software-enabled bricks and sustainability as attempts to sustain a recent period of stellar revenue and profit growth.
The toy firm – the largest of its kind globally – recently announced an increase in revenue of more than a fifth to a record DKr42bn (US$6.6bn) in the first half of the year, as net profit increased by a third to DKr8.6bn (US$1.34bn).
Lego’s CEO Niels Christiansen , who became chief executive in 2017, says Lego was taking market share in almost all countries and had broad-based growth through new products, including sets based on the FIFA World Cup, Formula 1 and Pokémon.
“We are really upping our investments. That is really the best insurance against what happened before,” Niels says, highlighting Lego’s brush with bankruptcy in 2004.
He adds: “If you forget to invest at the right rate, you may run out of steam sometime.”
